info.title: Nexus API
info.description: Control plane for the Nexus observability/BI platform: datasources, one-shot queries, live SSE streams, dashboards, panels, flows, and alerts.

Run the supplied input + pipeline against the bounded collector and return

post.summary:
Extract the request, bind its macros/variables, run it under the server
guards, return the rows. The dev single-datasource shortcut carries no
principal, so host tokens (`$caller_tenant_id`) are absent — a query needing
them errors, which is correct. The guards (read-only, timeout, caps) and the
binder live in the store; this handler only wires.

subject.description: Subject id of the acting principal.

oneOf.description:
An AI agent run. `run_id` is opaque to the changelog; consumers
with `starter-ai` join it themselves.

AgentDetail.description:
A configured agent in full. `config` is opaque JSON on the wire — the
provider/agent-specific knobs the nexus-ai facade interprets at run time.

backend.description: The facade backend: an inference provider hint or a coding-agent backend.

model.description: Concrete model id or a size alias ("small"/"medium"/"large").

AgentSummary.description:
An agent as it appears in the list: identity and backend/model, without the
config blob (that comes from the detail endpoint).

AlertCondition.description: One condition of an alert rule.

query.description: The query whose reduced first column is the evaluated value.

reducer.description: How the query's rows collapse to one value: last|min|max|avg|sum|count.

AlertEvent.description:
One recorded transition: when a rule fired or resolved, the value that
triggered it, and whether it was silenced / actually notified.

conditions.description:
The multi-condition list, when the rule uses one. `None` for a legacy
single-condition rule (its single condition is the top-level fields).

AssistRequest.description:
An assist request: a task, the user's natural-language intent, and optional
grounding context.

current_sql.description: Optional existing SQL to edit/improve rather than write from scratch.

datasource_id.description:
Optional datasource the query should target; when set, the server grounds
the model with that datasource's table/column schema so generated SQL
references real columns.

model.description:
Optional model override (concrete id or `small`/`medium`/`large`).
Defaults to the service's medium tier when omitted.

prompt.description: The user's plain-English ask (e.g. "average temperature per site, last 24h").

AssistResponse.description:
The assistant's structured answer. `result` shape depends on the request task
(see [`AssistTask`]); it is opaque JSON on the wire so the contract stays
stable as task outputs evolve. `raw` carries the model's unparsed reply for
debugging / when structured parsing degrades.

raw.description:
The model's raw text reply, retained so the UI can fall back to showing it
if the structured `result` is empty.

AssistTask.description:
What the caller wants the assistant to produce. The task selects the system
instructions and the expected shape of [`AssistResponse::result`].

Change.description:
A typed, append-only record of a single domain mutation.

Five product features collapse onto this primitive: user audit log,
AI-agent log, undo/redo, duplicate, and copy/paste. See
`DOCS/backend/undo-redo/SCOPE.md`.

after.description:
Snapshot of the row *after* the mutation. Used for redo,
duplicate, and paste.

before.description: Snapshot of the row *before* the mutation. Used for undo.

oneOf.description: Optional external trace id (HTTP request id, agent run id, …).

group_id.description:
Every change belongs to a group. Single-row mutations get a
fresh `GroupId`; multi-row transactions share one. Undo
operates on whole groups, so this is never `Option`.

patch.description:
Optional RFC 6902 patch document, as raw JSON. Kept as
[`serde_json::Value`] so this crate does not depend on a
patch-library crate — the backend picks one.

resource.description: Resource that was mutated. Kind + id (+ optional owner).

resource_version.description:
Optimistic-concurrency token taken at read time.
[`super::Reversible::apply_inverse`] uses it as the `WHERE`
predicate and returns [`crate::Error::Conflict`] if the row
has moved on. `None` for resources without versioning (caller
accepts last-write-wins).

ChangeId.description:
Identifier of a single row in `starter_changes`. ULID, monotonic
per recorder.

ChangePage.description: One page of changes plus the cursor for the next page.

next_cursor.description: Cursor to pass into the next [`ChangeFilter`]. `None` at end.

ColumnSchema.description: One column of a query result.

name.description: Column name as it appears in the result set.

CreateAgentRequest.description:
Create an agent. `backend` selects the facade tier/provider, `model` is a
concrete id or size alias. `config` carries provider-specific knobs and is
validated when a session runs, not here. `model` defaults to `large`.

CreateAlertRuleRequest.description:
Create an alert rule. A rule is either a legacy single condition (the
top-level `query`/`op`/`threshold`) or a multi-condition rule (`conditions`
combined by `combinator`). `no_data_policy`/`exec_error_policy` say how a
missing or failed evaluation resolves (`ok`|`alerting`|`keep_last`).

conditions.description: Multi-condition list; when set it supersedes the single `query`/`op`.

for_secs.description: Pending dwell in seconds before firing (0 = fire on first breach).

message_template.description: Optional notification message template; omitted uses the default.

CreateChannelRequest.description:
Create a notification channel. `kind` selects the delivery (webhook in v1);
`config` is the kind-specific settings (e.g. `{ "url": "…" }`).

CreateDashboardRequest.description:
Create a dashboard. The slug must be unique within the tenant; the server
rejects a duplicate rather than silently aliasing. Appearance (icon +
accent) is optional — omitted fields fall back to server defaults, so older
clients that send only name/slug keep working.

accent.description:
accent colour as an HSL triple string, e.g. "152 76% 44%"; defaults
server-side when omitted.

folder_id.description: Folder to file the dashboard under (WS-05); omit/`null` for the root.

icon.description: lucide icon name; defaults server-side when omitted.

CreateDatasourceRequest.description:
Body for creating a datasource. The `password` is write-only: it is accepted
here, envelope-encrypted at rest, and never echoed back by any read
endpoint.

name.description: Human-readable name shown in the datasource picker.

password.description: Write-only secret. Stored as ciphertext; absent from every response.

CreateFlowRequest.description:
Create a flow. `input`/`pipeline`/`output` are the ArkFlow config blobs; the
FlowManager validates them when it builds the stream, so a malformed config
surfaces on start, not here. `enabled` defaults to false so a flow can be
created and reviewed before it runs.

CreateFolderRequest.description:
Create a folder. `parent_id` files it under another folder (in the same
tenant); omit it for a root folder.

parent_id.description: Parent folder id; omit/`null` for a root folder.

CreatePanelRequest.description:
Create a panel under the dashboard named in the path. The dashboard is keyed
by its immutable id (resolved from the path slug at the request edge).

layout.description: Grid layout; defaults to empty when omitted.

viz.description: Visualization kind; defaults to `table` when omitted.

CreateSessionRequest.description:
Open a session against an agent by sending its opening prompt. The agent's
system prompt (if any) is prepended by the server; the caller supplies only
the user message. The response carries the session id whose SSE feed streams
the run.

CreateSessionResponse.description:
The response to opening a session: the session id (now `running`) plus a
short-lived signed token to connect its SSE feed at
`GET /api/v1/agents/sessions/{id}/events?token=…`. A browser `EventSource`
cannot set an auth header, so the token rides the query string.

token.description: Signed token for the SSE subscription.

CreateSilenceRequest.description:
Create a silence. `rule_id = None` silences every rule in the tenant for the
window; a value silences just that rule. Silencing suppresses notification,
not evaluation — the event history still records what fired.

CreateStreamRequest.description:
Body for creating a live stream: the datasource to read and the SQL shaping
applied to each batch before it is pushed to subscribers.

datasource_id.description: Datasource whose live input feeds this stream.

sql.description: SQL applied per batch (DataFusion pipeline) to shape the live rows.

CreateStreamResponse.description:
Result of creating a stream. The token is single-use-per-connection,
short-lived, and scoped to exactly this stream — it authorizes the SSE
subscription and nothing else.

expires_in_secs.description: Token lifetime in seconds; the client must connect before it expires.

subscribe_url.description: Relative URL to connect an `EventSource` to, with the token embedded.

token.description: Signed token to pass as `?token=` when opening the SSE connection.

CreateVariableRequest.description:
Create a dashboard variable. `name` is unique within the dashboard; a
duplicate is a conflict. The kind-specific authoring input rides in
`options_config` (opaque, shape owned by the UI).

name.description: Reference name without the `$`, unique per dashboard.

options_config.description: Kind-specific authoring config; defaults to an empty object.

DashboardDetail.description:
Full dashboard view: identity plus its ordered panels. The slug resolves to
the `id` at the request edge; everything below keys on the id.

accent.description: accent colour as an HSL triple string, e.g. "152 76% 44%".

folder_id.description: Folder this dashboard is filed under (WS-05); `null` is the root.

icon.description: lucide icon name for the sidebar/page chrome.

DashboardExport.description:
A self-contained, importable dashboard. Identity (`slug`/`name`) plus
appearance, its panels, and its variables.

schema_version.description: Model version; must match [`DASHBOARD_SCHEMA_VERSION`] to import.

DashboardSummary.description: A dashboard in a list: identity, route alias, display name, and appearance.

accent.description: accent colour as an HSL triple string, e.g. "152 76% 44%".

folder_id.description: Folder this dashboard is filed under (WS-05); `null` is the root.

icon.description: lucide icon name for the sidebar/page chrome.

id.description: Immutable id — grants and panel refs key on this.

DatasourceDetail.description:
Full datasource view. The connection is redacted — host/port/database/user
only, never the secret.

DatasourceKind.description:
The kind of datasource, which selects the ArkFlow input builder. v1 ships
SQL-over-Postgres as the first connector; the enum is the extension point as
more `register_input_builder` connectors land.

kinds.description: One entry per declared connector type.

DatasourceKindSummary.description:
One datasource-kind's catalogue entry: enough for the UI to render a config
form and know how the connector is tested, never the connector's internals.

config_schema.description:
The JSON Schema the connector's config validates against — the UI builds
its form from this.

description.description: Optional human description for the config form.

dialect.description:
The SQL dialect a query connector renders time macros in; absent for a
stream connector.

name.description: The kind id a datasource record stores (e.g. `postgres`, `mqtt`).

secret_fields.description:
Which config fields are secrets (sealed at rest, redacted on read). The UI
renders these as write-only password inputs.

surface.description:
Which query surface the connector serves: `query` (request → rows) or
`stream` (subscribe → events for live panels/flows).

test_mode.description:
How connectivity is tested before save: `query` (a probe query) or
`connect` (open + close a session).

DatasourceSchema.description: A datasource's introspected tables, for SQL autocomplete in the editor.

DatasourceSummary.description:
A datasource as it appears in a list — identity and kind only, no connection
detail. Use `GET /datasources/:id` for the redacted connection view.

id.description: Immutable datasource id (grants and panel refs key on this).

DateFormat.description:
Closed enum of date-format choices. Variants locked in stage 1.
*Revisit trigger:* a locale ships that none of these three formats
fit.

DryRunRequest.description:
Test a flow's `input` + `pipeline` without persisting it or running its real
output. The engine swaps in the bounded collector sink, runs the stream to
the first breached cap (or a short wall-clock deadline), and returns the
sample rows. `output` is intentionally absent — a dry run never writes to a
real sink. Optional `max_rows` lets the editor narrow the sample further
than the server default.

max_rows.description: Cap on sample rows; clamped to the server's hard maximum.

pipeline.description: The pipeline processors, in order. Defaults to an empty pipeline.

DryRunResponse.description:
A dry run's outcome. On a build/runtime failure `error` carries the message
and `rows` is empty; otherwise `rows`/`columns`/`stats` describe the bounded
sample (with `stats.truncated` set when a cap stopped the stream early).

columns.description: Column schema of the sample, derived from the result's Arrow schema.

error.description: A build or runtime error, surfaced before save. `None` on success.

stats.description: Row/byte/time counters and the truncation flag for the sample.

FlowDetail.description:
A saved ingestion flow in full. The three config blobs are opaque JSON on the
wire — the input connector, the processor pipeline, and the output sink the
FlowManager hands to the engine.

enabled.description: Whether the flow is configured to run.

metrics.description: Live run counters for this flow.

running.description: Whether the FlowManager currently has it running on this node.

FlowMetrics.description:
Live run state surfaced on the flows list and detail so an admin sees a
flow's health without opening it: whether it is running, when its current
(or most recent) run started, and the error that ended the last run (if
any). All fields reflect this node's in-process
[`FlowManager`](nexus_engine::FlowManager) state; they reset on restart and
are absent once the process restarts (single-node v1). Throughput counters
would require instrumenting every output sink, so they are intentionally
omitted rather than reported as zero.

last_error.description:
The error that ended the most recent run, or `None` if it ended cleanly
(or is still running).

last_started_at.description:
RFC-3339 timestamp of when the current or most recent run started, or
`None` if the flow has never run this process.

running.description: Whether the manager currently has the flow running on this node.

FlowSummary.description:
A flow as it appears in the list: identity and run state, without the config
blobs (those come from the detail endpoint).

metrics.description: Live run counters for this flow.

FolderSummary.description:
One folder: its immutable id, its parent (NULL = root), and display name. The
client assembles the tree from the flat list using `parent_id`.

parent_id.description: Parent folder id; `null` for a root folder.

ForgetRequest.description:
Which user to erase from the audit ledger. Erasure tombstones the *content*
(`before`/`after`/`patch`) of every change the subject authored, within the
caller's tenant; the audit fact (who/when/what op) is preserved, as a
regulator still needs to see that an action occurred.

subject.description: The principal subject (stable user id) whose authored changes to scrub.

ForgetResponse.description: Result of a forget request: how many ledger rows were tombstoned.

tombstoned.description: Number of ledger rows whose payloads were nulled.

GroupId.description:
Identifier shared by every [`super::Change`] recorded inside a
single [`super::ChangeRecorder::transaction`] call. Undo operates
on whole groups.

scopes.description: Fine-grained scope strings attached to the credential.

teams.description:
Team slugs the caller belongs to in the current tenant. Grants reference
teams by slug, so the SPA matches against these.

tenant_id.description:
Tenant the session is bound to. `None` for an unbound principal; `"*"`
marks a super-admin that bypasses the cross-tenant predicate.

NodeCategory.description:
Which palette group a node belongs to. The visual builder groups the palette
by this and constrains edges (input → processor* → output).

NodeType.description:
A node type the engine can build, described for the editor: its ArkFlow
`type` discriminant, palette grouping, labels, and a JSON Schema for its
config so the editor can render a schema-driven form instead of raw JSON.

config_schema.description: JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) for the node's config object.

kind.description: The ArkFlow `type` value the serialised graph node carries.

NodeTypeList.description:
The full palette: every registered node, in palette order (inputs,
processors, outputs).

NumberFormat.description:
Closed enum of number-format choices. Variants locked in stage 1.
*Revisit trigger:* Indian grouping (`1,23,456.78`) becomes a
shipped requirement.

oneOf.description:
Domain-specific operation. `String` (not `&'static str`)
because values are read back from `jsonb`.

custom.description:
Domain-specific operation. `String` (not `&'static str`)
because values are read back from `jsonb`.

PanelDetail.description:
A panel as the canvas renders it: which datasource + query feed it, how it is
drawn, and where it sits on the grid.

datasource_id.description: Datasource the panel queries. `None` if its datasource was deleted.

layout.description: Opaque grid layout the canvas owns.

sql.description: The panel's SQL, run under the server query guards when refreshed.

PanelExport.description:
One panel in the export — everything needed to re-create it bar the ids the
importing tenant mints fresh.

datasource_id.description:
Datasource this panel queries; `null` when the source dashboard had none
or the importing tenant should re-bind it.

PreferencesPatch.description:
`PATCH` body shape — mirror of [`super::ResolvedPreferences`] with
every field made optional.

Problem.description:
Machine-readable error body.

Mirrors RFC 7807 loosely. The `type` field is a stable string
identifier (`not_found`, `invalid_input`, …) that callers can
switch on; the HTTP status is set by the transport.

title.description: Short human title for the problem.

type.description:
Stable identifier for the error class. Matches lower-case
snake-case of [`crate::error::Error`] variants.

QueryHistoryEntry.description:
A past query run, as the recall drawer shows it. The `sql` is the authored
text so re-running it reproduces the original query.

datasource_id.description: The datasource queried, or absent for the dev single-source path.

elapsed_ms.description: Wall-clock execution time, when the run completed.

error.description: The error message, when the run failed.

row_count.description: Rows returned, when the run completed.

starred.description: Whether the user pinned this run.

QueryHistoryList.description: The history list response, newest (and starred) first.

QueryKindList.description: The registered query-kinds, name-ordered, for the editor's kind picker.

QueryKindSummary.description:
One registered query-kind's descriptive surface. The `params_schema` is the
kind's JSON Schema document, which a schema-driven form renders to collect
the named params the kind binds.

datasource_kind.description: The datasource shape the kind targets (e.g. `postgres`).

description.description: Human description for the picker, if the manifest declared one.

params_schema.description:
The kind's params JSON Schema — the contract a kind-mode request's
`params` validates against, and what a schema-driven form renders.

QueryRequest.description:
Body of a one-shot query. The caller supplies the SQL plus the optional
macro context (time range, variables) the server-side binder substitutes;
every safety bound (read-only role, statement timeout, forced `LIMIT`,
row/byte caps) is applied server-side and is deliberately *not* expressible
here — a client cannot raise its own limits, and every supplied value is
*bound* into the prepared statement, never inlined.

This is the C7 contract: a single owner (WS-03) for an endpoint several
workstreams feed. WS-01 fills `time_range`, WS-02 fills `variables`; both
flow through the same binder.

interval_secs.description:
The bucket width (seconds) for `$__timeGroup(col, $__interval)` and a
bare `$__interval`.

kind.description:
WS-10 kind-mode: the reverse-DNS id of a registered query-kind to run
*instead of* `sql`. When set, the server resolves the kind, validates
`params` against its schema, and binds the kind's own SQL — `sql` is
ignored. When absent (the default), the request is raw-SQL mode and `sql`
runs. This keeps `QueryRequest` a single additive contract (C7): kind-mode
is opt-in, sql-mode stays the default.

params.description:
WS-10 kind-mode named params, validated host-side against the kind's JSON
Schema before binding. Each value binds as a `$N` arg, never inlined.
Ignored in raw-SQL mode.

sql.description:
The SQL to run against the datasource. May carry macros (`$__timeFilter`)
and variable references (`$region`) the binder expands into bound args.
Pushed down to the source database so `WHERE`/`LIMIT` execute there.

oneOf.description:
The resolved absolute time window for `$__timeFilter`/`$__timeFrom`/
`$__timeTo`. Relative ranges (`now-6h`) are resolved client-side to
instants before sending so the bound query and the cache key agree.

variables.description:
Dashboard variable values, by name (without the leading `$`), expanded by
`$var` / `${var:csv}` / `$__sqlIn(var)`.

QueryResponse.description:
A completed query result: column schema, rows as JSON objects keyed by
column name, and execution stats. Rows are an array of objects rather than a
column-major frame because panels consume row records directly.

columns.description: Ordered column schema for the result set.

rows.description: One JSON object per row, keyed by column name.

stats.description: Execution metadata, including the `truncated` cap signal.

QueryStats.description:
Execution metadata returned alongside the rows. `truncated` is the signal a
caller needs: when `true` the result hit a server-enforced row/byte cap and
is incomplete — the caller must narrow the query rather than assume it saw
everything.

byte_count.description: Approximate serialized byte size of the returned rows.

row_count.description: Number of rows actually returned (after any cap).

truncated.description: `true` if a row/byte cap stopped the stream before it completed.

QueryTimeRange.description:
An absolute query window. Half-open (`from` inclusive, `to` exclusive),
matching the binder's `col >= from AND col < to` expansion.

QueryVariable.description:
One dashboard variable's resolved value(s). A single-valued variable carries
one entry; a multi-select carries several (expanded by `$__sqlIn`/`:csv`).

values.description:
One or more string values. Multiple values drive list expansion; the
binder binds each as its own argument so values are always inert.

RedactedConnection.description:
Connection details safe to return over the API: everything *except* the
secret. The password lives only as ciphertext in the store and is never
serialized here — `GET /datasources/:id` returns this redacted view.

has_secret.description:
Always `true` — present so the UI can show a "secret set" affordance
without ever receiving the secret itself.

ResolvedPreferences.description:
Fully-resolved per-principal preferences. All fields are concrete —
the resolver has already collapsed user → org → system → ICU
chains, so callers can trust every value.

currency.description:
ISO 4217 currency code (e.g. `"USD"`, `"EUR"`). Never `"auto"`
once resolved.

date_format.description: Concrete date format — never `Auto` once resolved.

language.description:
BCP-47 language subtag (e.g. `"en"`, `"fr"`). Drives i18n
message catalogue lookup.

locale.description:
BCP-47 locale tag (e.g. `"en-US"`, `"fr-FR"`). Drives ICU
formatting fallbacks.

number_format.description: Concrete number format — never `Auto` once resolved.

time_format.description: Concrete time format — never `Auto` once resolved.

timezone.description:
IANA timezone identifier (e.g. `"Europe/Paris"`,
`"America/New_York"`). Never `"auto"` once resolved.

unit_system.description:
`metric` or `imperial`. Drives per-unit `Auto` derivation
upstream; by the time it lands here the per-unit fields below
are already concrete, so this value is informational.

ResourceRef.description:
Reference to the object an authorization check is being made
against. `id == None` is a collection-level / route-level check
("may this user list flows at all?"); `id == Some(_)` is a
row-level check ("may this user update flow 42?").

`owner` is populated by the handler for row-level checks where
ownership matters — the engine can match
`principal.subject == object.owner` without a DB round-trip from
inside the engine. See SCOPE.md R5.

id.description:
Resource id for row-level checks. `None` for collection /
route-level checks.

kind.description:
Resource kind. Must be registered in the
[`super::ResourceRegistry`] (e.g. `"flows"`, `"users"`,
`"secrets"`).

owner.description: Subject id of the resource owner, if any.

tenant.description:
Tenant the resource row belongs to (Phase 7a — R11). For
kinds declared as `tenant_scoped = true` in the registry,
the engine requires
`Some(principal.tenant_id) == Some(object.tenant)` (with
the super-admin sentinel `"*"` bypassing the predicate).
`None` on a tenant-scoped kind is a `cross_tenant` deny —
the row is missing its tenancy column.

ResultColumnType.description:
The column's logical type, derived from the Arrow schema of the result.
Kept deliberately coarse — the frontend renders cells, it does not need the
full Arrow type lattice. Anything not in this set arrives as [`Self::Other`]
with the rows already JSON-encoded.

SchemaColumn.description:
One column: its name and declared SQL type (e.g. `timestamp`, `double
precision`).

SchemaTable.description: One table or view, schema-qualified, with its columns in declaration order.

schema.description: The Postgres schema the table lives in (e.g. `public`).

status.description: Lifecycle: pending | running | completed | failed | cancelled.

transcript.description: The message transcript: an array of `{role, content}` objects.

SetTagsRequest.description:
Body for `PUT …/tags` — the complete tag set to persist on an entity. This
is a full replace: tags not listed are removed, so the client sends the
whole set it wants, not a delta.

StarQueryRequest.description: Body of the star toggle: the desired pinned state for one history row.

StreamEvent.description:
One `data:` frame on a live stream. `seq` is the monotonic per-stream event
id echoed in the SSE `id:` field so a reconnecting client can send
`Last-Event-ID` to resume; `rows` is the batch shaped by the stream's SQL.

rows.description: The rows in this batch, one JSON object per row.

seq.description: Monotonic event sequence number within this stream.

Tag.description:
One tag: a `key` with an optional `value`. `value` absent (or null) is a
bare label; present is a key:value pair.

value.description: The tag value, e.g. `abc`. Absent for a bare label.

TaggableKind.description:
The kinds of entity that can be tagged. The set the API accepts — a tag's
target is referenced by kind + id, so a kind owned by another layer (a user,
a team) is taggable without this crate owning the entity. New variants are
add-only within a major.

TaggedEntity.description: An entity returned by a by-tag lookup: its kind and id.

id.description: The entity's id as a string (ids owned by other layers are not uuids).

TestConnectionRequest.description:
Body for a *pre-save* connection probe. Carries the same connection fields as
a create request, including the write-only secret, so the "Test connection"
affordance works before the datasource is persisted (and before a secret is
sealed). The secret is used transiently to connect and never stored or echoed.

password.description: Write-only secret used only to open the probe connection.

TestDatasourceResponse.description:
Outcome of a connection probe. `ok` is the headline; on failure `message`
carries the redacted reason (driver errors are sanitized so they never leak
the connection secret).

latency_ms.description: Round-trip latency of the probe in milliseconds, when it connected.

Theme.description:
Closed enum of UI theme choices. User-only field — the org-layer
Preferences DTO omits `theme` entirely. *Revisit trigger:* a
consumer needs org-enforced theming.

TimeFormat.description:
Closed enum of clock formats. Variants locked in stage 1.
*Revisit trigger:* none expected.

TraceId.description:
Correlation id linking a change to an external trace (HTTP request
id, agent run id, etc.). Opaque to the changelog.

UndoResponse.description:
The changelog group that an undo/redo applied. The client refreshes the
resources touched by this group (it can fetch the group's rows via the audit
API if it needs the per-resource detail).

group_id.description: The `group_id` that was undone or redone.

Unit.description:
Closed enum of unit codes for the v1 surface. Variants are locked
in stage 1 of the Phase 0 plan.

UnitSystem.description:
Closed enum of unit systems. Variants locked in stage 1 of the
Phase 0 plan. *Revisit trigger:* none expected — US-customary vs
Imperial nuance is handled in the per-unit derivation, not by
adding a third variant here.

UpdateAgentRequest.description: Partially update an agent; omitted fields are left unchanged.

UpdateAlertRuleRequest.description: Partially update an alert rule; omitted fields are unchanged.

UpdateDashboardRequest.description:
Partial update. Renaming the slug changes only the route alias — grants and
panel refs keep pointing at the immutable id, so nothing is orphaned. Moving
between folders and starring (WS-05) ride this same patch.

accent.description: accent HSL triple string; `None` leaves it unchanged.

folder_id.description:
Move into this folder. Ignored when `clear_folder` is true; `None` (with
`clear_folder` false) leaves the folder unchanged.

icon.description: lucide icon name; `None` leaves it unchanged.

UpdateDatasourceRequest.description:
Partial update. Every field is optional; `None` leaves the stored value
untouched. `password` follows the write-only rule — supplying it rotates the
secret, omitting it keeps the existing ciphertext.

password.description: Supplying a new secret rotates it; omitting it keeps the current one.

UpdateFlowRequest.description:
Partially update a flow; omitted fields are left unchanged. Toggling
`enabled` here does not by itself start/stop the flow — the dedicated
`start`/`stop` routes do that and also flip this flag — so a plain update is
for editing the config or name.

UpdateFolderRequest.description:
Partial update. `name` renames. The parent is three-valued, modelled
explicitly so a JSON-friendly wire shape (no double-`null` ambiguity) can
distinguish the cases: send `parent_id` to move under a folder, set
`clear_parent: true` to re-root, or send neither to leave the parent
unchanged. `clear_parent` wins if both are set.

clear_parent.description: Re-root the folder (set its parent to NULL).

parent_id.description: Move under this folder. Ignored when `clear_parent` is true.

UpdatePanelRequest.description: Partial update of a panel. `None` fields are left unchanged.

UpdateVariableRequest.description:
Partial update. Every field is optional — `None` leaves the stored value
untouched. Changing `current` alone is the common case (the user picked a new
value in the bar); changing the rest is the variable editor.

VariableDetail.description:
A dashboard variable definition. `options_config` carries the kind-specific
authoring input (the custom list, the option SQL + datasource, the interval
steps, or the datasource-kind filter); it is opaque on the wire because its
shape varies by `kind` and the UI owns each shape. `current` holds the
selected value(s); the binder receives these (resolved) as `QueryVariable`.

current.description:
Currently selected value(s). One entry for a single-select; several for a
multi-select / "All" expansion. The binder binds each as its own arg.

hidden.description: Whether the variable is hidden from the bar (constants usually are).

include_all.description: Whether an "All" option is offered (expands to every resolved option).

label.description: Human label for the variable bar; falls back to `name` when absent.

multi.description: Whether multiple values may be selected at once.

name.description: The reference name without the `$` (e.g. `region`). Unique per dashboard.

options_config.description: Kind-specific authoring config (opaque; shape owned by the UI per kind).

sort_order.description:
Display/resolution order within the dashboard's variable bar; lower
sorts first. Ties break by creation order.

VariableExport.description:
One variable in the export. Mirrors the relational variable row minus its
ids; opaque `options_config` travels as-is.

VariableKind.description:
The kind of a dashboard variable — what populates its option list and how its
value is sourced. Mirrors Grafana's templating types; the UI resolves the
options for each kind, the binder only ever sees the *resolved* string
value(s) (WS-03's `$var`/`$__sqlIn` expansion).

WeekStart.description:
Closed enum of week-start choices. Variants locked in stage 1.
*Revisit trigger:* a locale that starts the week on Saturday (parts
of MENA) surfaces as a shipped requirement.
